Yael Mizrahi is a Backend Engineer at Sentinel Cybersecurity Solutions, where he specializes in building secure, scalable infrastructure for threat detection systems. As a skip-level manager, I’ve observed his contributions through cross-team collaborations and project outcomes, not direct daily oversight. His work is rooted in solving complex security challenges with precision and pragmatism.  

Yael’s technical depth is evident in his architecture of microservices for real-time intrusion detection, which reduced false positives by 32% through fine-grained access controls. He leveraged Go to develop high-performance security modules, handling 10M+ requests/sec with sub-50ms latency. His AWS expertise optimized cost structures for cloud-based security analytics, cutting spend by 18% while maintaining 99.99% uptime. He also designed REST APIs that integrated with third-party threat intelligence feeds, enabling automated response workflows. PostgreSQL underpins his data pipelines, where he engineered query optimizations that slashed report generation time by 40%.  

Beyond code, Yael’s adaptability shines. He mentored junior engineers during a critical SOC incident, guiding them to isolate a zero-day exploit in under an hour. His curiosity drives him to dissect security vulnerabilities, often proposing proactive measures ahead of compliance audits.  

Yael’s work has fortified Sentinel’s security posture, enabling faster threat response and reducing remediation delays by 25%. I recommend him without hesitation for roles requiring both technical rigor and strategic foresight. His metrics-driven approach and ethical rigor make him a rare asset in cybersecurity.
